alerts.title: Carbamazepine co-prescribed with DTG may lower DTG levels and cause virologic failure
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases dolutegravir levels by 30-70% and recommend using valproic acid instead. The patient takes DTG-based TLD together with carbamazepine (started 2 weeks ago) and valproate. Viral load is now detectable at 1,240 copies/mL from <50 copies/mL in 2025-09-01, despite reported good adherence. The timing of carbamazepine initiation and the viral load rise are consistent with this interaction, though adherence and other causes have not been excluded. The clinician's plan reduces carbamazepine but does not address the DTG interaction or the viral load rise.

evidence.recommended_action: Avoid carbamazepine with DTG; use valproic acid as the anti-epileptic. Repeat viral load in 2-3 months with enhanced adherence support, and consider ART regimen review.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load requires repeat testing and adherence/side-effect assessment
alerts.message: Guidelines state that if viral load is above 50 copies/mL, enhanced adherence support should be provided, side effects affecting adherence addressed, and viral load repeated in 2-3 months. Viral load is 1,240 copies/mL today versus <50 copies/mL 176 days ago. Adherence is reported as good, but the cause is unclear and the clinician's plan does not include a repeat viral load.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, address drug side effects affecting adherence, and repeat viral load in 2-3 months.

alerts.title: Hyponatraemia and carbamazepine-related neurotoxicity; confirm regimen review
alerts.message: Sodium is 128 mmol/L with headache, dizziness, unsteady gait, nystagmus and tremor, alongside a carbamazepine level of 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic range 4-12). These findings are consistent with carbamazepine toxicity, which can cause hyponatraemia, though other causes were not documented in the excerpts. The excerpts do not give a specific sodium threshold, so this alert relies on the clinical picture rather than a guideline rule.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine as planned, repeat the level and sodium, and review the anti-epileptic choice with neurology given the DTG interaction.
